intro.title: Build usage quota tracking and enforcement
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple usage quota tracker and enforcer for a Node.js application. You will learn how to monitor and limit the number of times a specific action, like an API call, can be performed by a user. The core programming concept involves using a counter variable to track usage and conditional logic to enforce limits. You will work with basic JavaScript constructs like variables, if/else statements, and functions. By the end, you'll have a functional quota system that can block further actions once a limit is reached.
intro.usecase: Usage quota tracking is essential in SaaS platforms where customers pay based on consumption, like API services (Stripe, Twilio) that limit monthly requests. Developers implement this in billing dashboards showing usage meters, quota warnings, and upgrade prompts. This pattern also appears in cloud platforms (AWS, Google Cloud) that enforce resource limits and display usage analytics panels. Understanding quota enforcement helps build fair billing systems and prevent service abuse.
